title: Derived local morphism and isomorphism presheaves
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be an essentially small site with objects in $\mathrm{Type}(u+1)$ and morphisms in $\mathrm{Type}(u)$, and let $B$ be a commutative ring in $\mathrm{Type}(u+1)$. Use module-valued sheaves $\operatorname{Sh}(J,\operatorname{Mod}_B)$, the constant-coefficient encoding of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and the actual derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $U\in\mathcal C$, localization uses $J/U$, restriction of sheaves, and relocalization along $V\to U$ as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Write $r_U$ and $r_f$ for their exact functors induced on derived categories, and $r_U(-)|_V\cong r_V(-)$ for the canonical restriction isomorphism. For derived objects $A,D$, define presheaves $P_{A,D}(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(J/U,B)}(r_U A,r_U D)$ and $Q_{A,D}(U)=\operatorname{Isom}_{D(J/U,B)}(r_U A,r_U D)$. Restriction is the image under $r_f$, conjugated by these canonical isomorphisms; it obeys the identity and composition laws. Define $\mathcal H_{A,D}=P_{A,D}^{\#}$ and $\mathcal I_{A,D}=Q_{A,D}^{\#}$ by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Composition on each is the unique map from the product of the corresponding sheaves that agrees with composition of actual local morphisms or isomorphisms after the sheafification units. Precomposition and postcomposition induce their canonical maps; for $\mathcal I$ the changes of arguments are isomorphisms. There is the canonical map $\mathcal I\to\mathcal H$ forgetting the inverse.

For another commutative ring $B'$, a coherent localized functor consists of a functor $T:D(J,B)\to D(J,B')$, functors $T_U:D(J/U,B)\to D(J/U,B')$, and natural isomorphisms $r_U T\cong T_U r_U$ (written in the direction $r_U(-)$ followed by $T_U$ to $T(-)$ followed by $r_U$), such that the induced conjugated maps on both local Hom and local Isom commute with every restriction. These data induce maps on $P,Q,\mathcal H,\mathcal I$. Restriction of scalars along $B\to B'$ commutes with localization by the identity comparison on sheaves and its induced derived isomorphism. This specifies all functoriality data; it does not replace actual derived morphisms by underived maps.
